bug_semantics: An administrator or authenticated caller with connect-write authority can persist an attacker-chosen ConnectURL. The public GET /api/connects/info path, and later the authenticated connection-health path, cause the server to append /api/connect and issue an unrestricted outbound HTTP request to that stored URL. Because the request primitive performs no URL, resolved-address, redirect, loopback, private-network, or link-local/cloud-metadata validation, the caller can make the Ech0 server reach internal services and metadata endpoints and return or infer their responses.
flaw_origin: fabee479ccf98c081bb065926c726b461a42fdf3 first moved peer-detail retrieval from the browser into the server: it added publicRoutes.GET("/connects/info", controllers.GetConnectsInfo), GetConnectsInfo's iteration over stored ConnectURL values, and pkg.SendRequest implemented with an unconstrained http.Client.Do. The same commit therefore created both the server-side attacker-controlled request and the missing trust-boundary validation; later copies, retries, health checks, rewrites, and the fetchPeerConnectInfo extraction preserved rather than originated that mechanism.
ai_marker: absent: the raw commit object for fabee479ccf98c081bb065926c726b461a42fdf3 has author and committer L1nSn0w <l1nsn0w@qq.com> and message 'feat: 添加获取 Connect 信息的功能，并更新相关路由和常量'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/security/advisories/GHSA-8mc6-xjpr-h98x identifies fetchPeerConnectInfo in internal/service/connect/connect.go, the unsafe SendRequest call, private/cloud-metadata reachability, and patched version 4.7.3. At vulnerable tag v4.7.2 (88a564fcdd1ca0fbeecd75ed5f522df95372d308), internal/router/connect.go registers public GET /connects/info, authenticated scope-protected GET /connects/health, and authenticated connect-write POST /connects; AddConnect only rejects empty URLs, trims them, checks duplicates, and stores them, while fetchPeerConnectInfo at internal/service/connect/connect.go:219-227 appends /api/connect and calls httpUtil.SendRequest. `git log -L 219,227:internal/service/connect/connect.go v4.7.2` leads to extraction commit 2d1698c515ebdd3945c30b22f17e517893a4be9a, whose diff removes equivalent SendRequest blocks from the info and health paths, proving it is only a refactor. Following the pre-extraction info block with `git log -L 282,288:internal/service/connect/connect.go 1b8c64d0...` reaches the v2 rewrite d87ddc2085435189b969cffbdc5f87640e6e7929; its immediate predecessor retains the equivalent implementation under Ech0_OLD. Commit 397fc6fc46cceaa02a745cc51d8e58b78a8edcc2 is a 100% rename of internal/services/connect_service.go to Ech0_OLD/internal/services/connect_service.go. Continuing `git log -L 144,158:Ech0_OLD/internal/services/connect_service.go 397fc6...` reaches fabee479ccf98c081bb065926c726b461a42fdf3, whose patch first adds pkg.SendRequest, server-side GetConnectsInfo, and public /connects/info. Direct parent-tree command `git grep -n -e GetConnectsInfo -e SendRequest -e '/connects/info' 4e343d6638b14e535a8fda2c258724527ff533e4 -- internal/controllers/connect.go internal/routers/routers.go internal/services/connect_service.go pkg/other.go` returns no matches, while the BIC patch adds all of them. The parent is tag v1.2.8; `git tag --contains fabee479... --sort=version:refname` shows the first v-series release containing the BIC is v1.2.9, refining the repository advisory's broad 'all versions' lower bound. Fix 091d26d2d942df6df9f520328d2f9cf2592bbefc changes fetchPeerConnectInfo to SendSafeRequest and validates ConnectURL + /api/connect before insertion; SendSafeRequest invokes ValidatePublicHTTPURL and SecureDialContext. `git tag --contains 091d26d...` starts at v4.7.3 (and not v4.7.2); v4.7.3 peels to release commit 6ad621d8d461c58f1a1d179c4dfbb741803f8aa5, which contains the direct fix.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins at fabee479ccf98c081bb065926c726b461a42fdf3, not at the much later fetchPeerConnectInfo refactor. Before the BIC, users could store connection URLs and the browser could contact peers, but the Ech0 server had no GetConnectsInfo outbound-request path. The BIC added an unauthenticated trigger that reads the stored values and an unconstrained server-side HTTP client in one small commit. The mechanism survived concurrency/retry changes, the 100% old-tree relocation, the large v2 rewrite, and later extraction into fetchPeerConnectInfo; c167476d70c85710e240dbdf019b44d3fb5abe21 added a second health-check trigger without being the first origin. Immediate-parent grep against the parent tree establishes absence of the endpoint, service function, and request primitive, and release ancestry puts the first affected v-series tag at v1.2.9. The direct fix 091d26d2d942df6df9f520328d2f9cf2592bbefc closes both sides of the flaw by rejecting unsafe URLs at insertion and using the already-hardened request path at fetch time, and it is present from v4.7.3. Because the only admissible AI-attribution source is the smallest BIC's raw commit object, and that object contains only the human L1nSn0w identity with no AI authorship/co-authorship marker, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
